record.paper_title: TWISTED GGP PROBLEMS AND CONJECTURES, GGP IV
record.original_question: Establish the vanishing assumption for generalized Steinberg representations that the two branching spaces Hom_{U(V+V)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+V,ψ,μ}) and Hom_{U(V+W)}(Sp(π,2), ω_{V+W,ψ,μ}) are both zero for the two isomorphism classes V and W of m-dimensional skew-Hermitian spaces over E. The paper identifies this as a special case of the nontempered twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad conjecture and explicitly says it does not know how to prove it except when m = 1.

evidence.quote: To deal with the generalised Steinberg representations, we will need to make an assumption. ... (Assumption) Hom_{U(V+V)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+V,ψ,μ}]=0, Hom_{U(V+W)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+W,ψ,μ}]=0.
At the moment, we do not know how to prove the (Assumption) that Hom_{U(V^2)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V^2,ψ}] = Hom_{U(V+W)}[Sp(π,2),ω_{V+W,ψ}] = 0, except when m = dim V = dim W = 1.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E/F$ be a quadratic extension of non-archimedean local fields of characteristic zero, with nontrivial Galois automorphism $c$. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi: F \to \mathbb{C}^\times$ and a character $\mu$ of $E^\times$ whose restriction to $F^\times$ is the quadratic character associated to $E/F$.

For each positive integer $m$, there are exactly two isomorphism classes of non-degenerate $m$-dimensional skew-Hermitian spaces over $E$; denote representatives by $V$ and $W$. For any skew-Hermitian space $X$ over $E$, let $U(X)$ denote its unitary group and let $\omega_{X,\psi,\mu}$ denote the associated Weil representation of $U(X)$ (with respect to the splitting data $(\psi,\mu)$) on the doubled space, viewed as a smooth representation.

Let $\pi$ be a tempered irreducible smooth representation of $U(V)$, and let $\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2)$ denote the generalized Steinberg representation of $U(V \oplus V)$ (respectively $U(V \oplus W)$) associated to $\pi$, defined as the unique irreducible quotient (Langlands quotient) of the parabolically induced representation $\mathrm{Ind}_{P}^{U(V \oplus V)}(\pi |\det|^{1/2})$ for the Siegel-type parabolic $P$, normalized so that it generalizes the Steinberg representation when $\pi$ is the trivial character.

Prove that for every such $\pi$ and for both isomorphism classes $V$ and $W$,
$$\mathrm{Hom}_{U(V\oplus V)}\!\big(\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2),\; \omega_{V\oplus V,\psi,\mu}\big) = 0 \qquad \text{and} \qquad \mathrm{Hom}_{U(V\oplus W)}\!\big(\mathrm{Sp}(\pi,2),\; \omega_{V\oplus W,\psi,\mu}\big) = 0.$$

Equivalently, establish this vanishing in all dimensions $m = \dim V = \dim W \geq 1$ (the case $m=1$ being known).
artifact.status_search_result: The vanishing assumption for generalized Steinberg representations within the twisted Gan-Gross-Prasad framework is explicitly noted as known only for $m=1$. Recent work on the twisted GGP conjecture (e.g., results on central values of Asai L-functions) addresses the conjecture under local assumptions but does not appear to remove this Steinberg-type vanishing hypothesis. No source verifying a full proof for $m \geq 2$ was found.

status_evidence.title: Twisted GGP Problems and Conjectures (arXiv)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the nontempered twisted GGP conjecture and identifies the vanishing assumption for generalized Steinberg representations as a special case not known beyond m=1.
status_evidence.claim: The assumption is stated as unproven except when m = 1.

status_evidence.title: Central values of Asai L-functions and twisted Gan–Gross–Prasad conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work proves cases of the twisted GGP conjecture under local assumptions; the Steinberg vanishing assumption is not removed.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work on twisted GGP still relies on or does not resolve this vanishing in general.
